identity.title: Learning Dynamics in Continual Pre-Training for Large Language Models

problem.claim: Characterize how general and downstream-domain performance evolves at each step of continual pre-training for LLMs, using validation losses as domain-performance measures.

contributions.claim: A decomposition of the CPT loss curve into distribution-shift and learning-rate-annealing effects.
A CPT scaling law combining distribution shift and learning-rate effects to predict loss across continual-training steps and learning-rate schedules.
A formulation for relating learning rate, training steps, and PT–CPT dataset distance, with proposed hyperparameter customization for balancing general and domain-specific performance.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a CPT scaling law that jointly accounts for distribution shift and learning-rate annealing and predicts losses across training steps and schedules.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that the CPT loss curve characterizes a transition between an initial curve and a hidden curve, explainable by decoupling distribution shift from learning-rate annealing.
The authors report that extensive experiments support the scaling law across various CPT datasets and hyperparameters.

narrative_sequence.summary: CPT is framed as a popular approach for adapting foundation models to downstream tasks.
The work examines learning dynamics during CPT, tracking general and downstream-domain validation losses at each training step.
The authors describe CPT loss evolution as a transition between curves shaped by distribution shift and learning-rate annealing.
They derive a combined scaling law for loss prediction across steps and learning-rate schedules, and report broad experimental support.

source_observation.claim: The abstract separates distribution shift and learning-rate annealing before combining them in a loss-prediction law.

lessons.interpretation: Separating interacting factors can make a training-dynamics claim more interpretable and actionable.
lessons.application: When proposing a training scaling law, model major data and optimization effects separately, then state how their combination yields predictions or tuning rules.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the factors cannot be independently identified or when the target behavior is not measurable through a comparable loss.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the scaling-law form, prediction accuracy, datasets, model sizes, training-step ranges, or learning-rate schedules.
The meaning and empirical construction of the referenced hidden curve is not detailed.
The reported experiments do not provide quantitative comparisons or uncertainty information.
